null_conical.label: $\phi = 0$
null_conical.input: The string's own travelling wave, $F = -2\ell(br/\ell)^{1/b}(A''\cos\phi + B''\sin\phi)$, for the pulse $A = (\ell/2)\,e^{-4u^2/\ell^2}$, $B = 0$ on a string with $b = 1/2$, whose cone lacks half a turn.
caption: The plane of $u$ and $v$ ($r = \ell$, $\phi = 0$), on the side of the string its displacement $A$ points to, drawn with $z = (v - u)/2$ and $ct = (u + v)/2$. The rays moving right keep their $u$ and travel with the wave. A curve moving left crosses the wave with $dv/du = F$, and here $F = -\tfrac{1}{2}\ell A''$: it keeps $v + \tfrac{1}{2}\ell A'$, so it is moved along $v$ while the string accelerates and comes out of the pulse where it would have been without it.

The rays moving right are null geodesics. $\Gamma^r{}_{uu} = -\partial_rF/2$ turns light crossing the wave out of this plane, so a curve moving left is a null curve, and a null geodesic only outside the pulse.

null_conical.label: $\phi = \pi$
null_conical.input: The string's own travelling wave, $F = -2\ell(br/\ell)^{1/b}(A''\cos\phi + B''\sin\phi)$, for the pulse $A = (\ell/2)\,e^{-4u^2/\ell^2}$, $B = 0$ on a string with $b = 1/2$, whose cone lacks half a turn.
caption: The plane of $u$ and $v$ ($r = \ell$, $\phi = \pi$), on the side of the string its displacement $A$ points away from, drawn with $z = (v - u)/2$ and $ct = (u + v)/2$. The rays moving right keep their $u$ and travel with the wave. A curve moving left crosses the wave with $dv/du = F$, and here $F = \tfrac{1}{2}\ell A''$: it keeps $v - \tfrac{1}{2}\ell A'$, so it is moved along $v$ while the string accelerates and comes out of the pulse where it would have been without it.

The rays moving right are null geodesics. $\Gamma^r{}_{uu} = -\partial_rF/2$ turns light crossing the wave out of this plane, so a curve moving left is a null curve, and a null geodesic only outside the pulse.

isotropic.label: $x = \ell/4$
isotropic.input: The pulse $A = (\ell/2)\,e^{-4u^2/\ell^2}$, $B = 0$ on a string with $b = 1/2$, whose cone lacks half a turn.
caption: The plane of $u$ and $v$ ($x = \ell/4$, $y = 0$), at a fixed isotropic distance from the string, drawn with $z = (v - u)/2$ and $ct = (u + v)/2$. The chart moves with the string, so the wave shows on this plane as $g_{uu} = -2xA''$ alone. The rays moving right keep their $u$ and travel with the wave, and a curve moving left keeps $v + 2xA'$.

The rays moving right are null geodesics. $\Gamma^x{}_{uu} = (\rho/\ell)^{2 - 2b}A''$ turns light crossing the wave out of this plane, so a curve moving left is a null curve, and a null geodesic only outside the pulse.

moving_string.label: $X = -\ell/4$
moving_string.input: The pulse $A = (\ell/2)\,e^{-4u^2/\ell^2}$, $B = 0$ on a string with $b = 1/2$, whose cone lacks half a turn.
caption: The plane of $u$ and $V$ ($X = -\ell/4$, $Y = 0$), a line parallel to the string's resting place, drawn with $z = (V - u)/2$ and $ct = (u + V)/2$. The pulse carries the string from $X = 0$ out to $\ell/2$ and back, between $\ell/4$ and $3\ell/4$ from this line. On this plane $g_{uu} = ((\rho/\ell)^{2b - 2} - 1)A'^2$, positive inside $\rho = \ell$, so the cones lean toward $+z$ on either side of the crest, where the string is moving, and stand at 45° on the crest and away from the pulse.

The rays moving right keep their $u$, travel with the wave, and are null geodesics. A curve moving left is moved along $V$ by $\int g_{uu}\,du = 0.65\,\ell$ in crossing the pulse. Light crossing the wave is turned out of this plane, so that curve is a null curve, and a null geodesic only outside the pulse.

moving_string.label: $X = 3\ell/4$
moving_string.input: The pulse $A = (\ell/2)\,e^{-4u^2/\ell^2}$, $B = 0$ on a string with $b = 1/2$, whose cone lacks half a turn.
caption: The plane of $u$ and $V$ ($X = 3\ell/4$, $Y = 0$), a line parallel to the string's resting place, drawn with $z = (V - u)/2$ and $ct = (u + V)/2$. The pulse carries the string from $X = 0$ out to $\ell/2$ and back, coming within $\ell/4$ of this line. On this plane $g_{uu} = ((\rho/\ell)^{2b - 2} - 1)A'^2$, positive inside $\rho = \ell$, so the cones lean toward $+z$ on either side of the crest, where the string is moving, and stand at 45° on the crest and away from the pulse.

The rays moving right keep their $u$, travel with the wave, and are null geodesics. A curve moving left is moved along $V$ by $\int g_{uu}\,du = 0.78\,\ell$ in crossing the pulse. Light crossing the wave is turned out of this plane, so that curve is a null curve, and a null geodesic only outside the pulse.
